reason: The cited evidence supports the general use of CALPHAD for HEAs (E1, E3) and the role of configurational entropy (E2, E4), but no passage provides specific prior results demonstrating that DSC, dilatometry, and an updated CALPHAD framework have been combined to achieve the claimed quantitative accuracy for melting properties across the HEA family.
premises: DSC can accurately measure latent heat and heat capacity jumps at the HEA melting transition
Dilatometry can accurately quantify volumetric expansion at the HEA melting transition
CALPHAD models can be updated to incorporate configurational entropy contributions for HEAs
Combining DSC, dilatometry, and updated CALPHAD yields synergistic predictions of melting parameters
The integrated approach achieves ±10 K accuracy for melting temperature and ±5–10% for fusion enthalpy/entropy
